I can’t determine whether Alex has cancer from that sentence. Inferring a specific health condition from “I have an appointment at the hospital next week” would require assuming sensitive medical information that isn’t present.

Helpful next steps instead:
- Prepare a contingency staffing plan that doesn’t assume severity (e.g., temporary coverage, shift swaps, cross-training, or on-call backup).
- Ask Alex a neutral, privacy-respecting question to clarify any staffing impact. Example message you can send:
  - “Hi Alex — I hope all is well. Do you expect to need any time off or schedule changes next week so we can plan coverage? We’re happy to accommodate as needed.”
- If Alex indicates a health issue, involve HR or your EAP to handle accommodations confidentially and in line with policy/law.
- Keep any health-related information confidential and only share it with those who need to know.

If you’d like, I can draft a short message to Alex tailored to your tone and company policy or outline a contingency staffing plan template. Which would you prefer?
